argument_assessments.reason: GPS records arrival at 10:00 and cancellation at 10:04. Fare evidence computes four elapsed minutes, with neither the five-minute free wait nor the eight-minute no-show threshold reached.
GPS supports arrival and four minutes at the bay, but the driver's inability to see the rider does not establish the required wait.
GPS supports presence during the four-minute wait and chat records both the driver's messages and the rider's reply. Those facts do not establish that the trip's no-show threshold was reached.
The rider correctly identifies a cancellation before either trip waiting threshold, which the driver acknowledges.

judge.policy_fit_reason: R-02 and D-02 support reviewing pickup coordination and accurate trip status; R-03 and D-03 support charge review. The waiting thresholds come from the trip's fare evidence, not the shared policy text, and were not reached.
judge.reasoning_summary: The four-minute wait ended before the trip's five-minute free wait and eight-minute no-show threshold. The rider replied that they were coming; their physical location is unknown. Arrival and contact do not justify the premature no-show charge. Uphold the claim and reverse the cancellation fee recorded in the fare evidence.
judge.precedent_departure: PREC-NS-05 and PREC-NS-01 rejected the claim because the no-show threshold had been reached. Here only four minutes had passed, below both the free wait and the threshold.
